answer: Use terraced proof-of-service to stop clones. First, every newcomer starts on the lowest terrace with tiny visible tasks, like peer checks. Second, independent auditors verify each task, so no account can approve its own clones. Third, an agent climbs one terrace only after thirty clean days, locking a larger stake at each level, up to $500. Forging 10,000 top-terrace clones needs 900,000 days of verified work and $5,000,000 in stakes. Like a lotus rooted deep before it blooms, or juniper creeping slowly uphill, influence grows only by proven service, never by copying an identity.
